TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Sampling Steps on Diffusion-based Image Fusion
PROPOSAL: This experiment compares the performance of a pre-trained diffusion model on the multi-focus image fusion task for a range of sampling steps (1, 5, 10, 50, 100) using the popular K/DA-L10K dataset, with metrics including PSNR, SSIM, and MMCE. Controls will include a traditional multi-focus image fusion approach (e.g., PCA-based fusion) and ablating the model by comparing against a diffusion model with a fixed, small number of steps (e.g., 5) but without fine-tuning.
CONTROLS: MS-FSV [1], A3T [2], PCA based fusion [3]
COST: 24 GPU-hours (10k iterations of model sampling and evaluation for each sampling step)
PREDICTION: We expect PSNR and SSIM scores to drop significantly when reducing the sampling steps from 100 to 50, and again when reducing to 10. However, a sampling step of 5 might still achieve competitive results, but potentially with reduced MMCE, indicating a trade-off between visual quality and information content.

References:
[1] Multi-scale fusion algorithm for image fusion.
[2] Fusion cross task transfer.
[3] PCA based algorithm.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Effectiveness of Knowledge Distillation for Accelerating Diffusion-based Image Fusion
PROPOSAL: This experiment compares the performance of a pre-trained diffusion model (e.g., u-diffusion V2 [4]) on multi-exposure image fusion with and without knowledge distillation (KD) training, using the multi-exposure image fusion dataset of Kee et al. [5]. KD will be implemented using the model's own latent space, and the teacher model will be the pre-trained diffusion model. Controls will include ablating the KD training and evaluating the teacher model's performance on the same task.
CONTROLS: Ablation of KD, pre-trained diffusion model (teacher)
COST: 40 GPU-hours (training a teacher-student pair with KD for 10k iterations)
PREDICTION: We expect the KD-trained student model to achieve competitive results with the teacher model in terms of PSNR and SSIM scores, but with a significant reduction in computational cost required for image fusion. However, the KD-trained model might not generalize as well as the teacher model to other fusion tasks.

References:
[4] Daali et al. “Energy-based diffusion models”
[5] Kee et al. (2018), Exposure fusion

Assuming the generalization of diffusion model in fusion domain and multi-exposure dataset is enough to start the exploration.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Investigating the Effectiveness of Knowledge Distillation for Accelerating Diffusion-based Image Fusion
PROPOSAL: This experiment is revised to include a multi-task learning setup, where the student model is fine-tuned on the multi-exposure image fusion dataset of Kee et al. [5] and then evaluated on a variety of fusion tasks, including multi-focus and infrared-visible image fusion, using the K/DA-L10K dataset. Extra controls will be added to compare against a student model fine-tuned on the individual tasks separately.
CONTROLS: Ablation of KD, pre-trained diffusion model (teacher), KD-trained student model fine-tuned separately on each task, KD-trained student model fine-tuned only on multi-exposure image fusion.
COST: 80 GPU-hours (training and fine-tuning multiple teacher-student pairs with KD across various tasks)
PREDICTION: We expect the KD-trained student model fine-tuned on the multi-exposure image fusion dataset to generalize well across various fusion tasks, achieving competitive results with the teacher model in terms of PSNR and SSIM scores. The student model fine-tuned separately on individual tasks might not generalize as well, but fine-tuning on multi-exposure image fusion might lead to a good compromise between task-specific performance and generalization.

Assuming in this turn, multi-task learning for KD will be sufficient and check the multi-exposure inference ability.

TITLE: Investigating the Effectiveness of Knowledge Distillation for Accelerating Diffusion-based Image Fusion
PROPOSAL: This experiment is revised to include a comparison with a state-of-the-art image fusion method, specifically the popular approach of Yu et al. [6] which uses a coupled U-Net architecture. The KD-trained student model will be compared against this approach on the same tasks and dataset. Additionally, we will evaluate the information-theoretic quantities such as mutual information to measure the fusion quality.
CONTROLS: Ablation of KD, pre-trained diffusion model (teacher), KD-trained student model fine-tuned on the multi-exposure image fusion dataset, state-of-the-art coupled U-Net approach [6]
COST: 120 GPU-hours (training and fine-tuning the KD-trained model, evaluating the coupled U-Net approach, and computing the information-theoretic quantities)
PREDICTION: We expect the KD-trained student model to achieve competitive results with the state-of-the-art coupled U-Net approach in terms of PSNR and SSIM scores, while providing a significant reduction in computational cost. The mutual information analysis will provide insights into the underlying information-theoretic characteristics of the fusion process.

Reference:
[6] Yu et al. (2020), Coupled U-net for image fusion.

This revised proposal allows us to compare the KD-trained model with a state-of-the-art approach, while also exploring the fusion quality from the information-theoretic perspective.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Latent-Space Representations for Diffusion-based Image Fusion
PROPOSAL: This experiment explores the concept of using pre-trained Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) to generate suitable latent-space representations for image fusion, leveraging the reconstruction-oriented objectives to learn modalities-specific features. We will evaluate the performance of VAE-based latent-space representations in conjunction with a pre-trained diffusion model on the multi-exposure image fusion task using the Kee et al. [5] dataset. Controls will include ablating the VAE-based latent-space representations and comparing against a diffusion model without any latent-space manipulation.
CONTROLS: Ablation of VAE-based latent-space representations, pre-trained diffusion model without latent-space manipulation
COST: 32 GPU-hours (training and fine-tuning a VAE model on the dataset, evaluating the joint performance)
PREDICTION: We expect the diffusion model combined with VAE-based latent-space representations to achieve improved fusion performance in terms of PSNR and SSIM scores, as the VAE model is able to capture modalities-specific features during reconstruction. However, the automatic early stop during the fusion process may in some cases leads to poor performance.

TITLE: Evaluating the Robustness of Diffusion-based Image Fusion to Noisy Observation
PROPOSAL: This experiment evaluates the robustness of diffusion-based image fusion to noisy observation, by adding synthetic noise to the source images and assessing the performance of the KD-trained student model on the multi-exposure image fusion task using the Kee et al. [5] dataset. We will study the effects of noise levels on the fusion performance, and explore the use of noise estimation techniques to improve the robustness of the diffusion model.
CONTROLS: Ablation of noise addition, pre-trained diffusion model with no noise estimation
COST: 48 GPU-hours (evaluating the diffusion model on noisy source images with varying noise levels, noise estimation and analysis)
PREDICTION: We expect the KD-trained student model to be relatively robust to moderate levels of noise, but to degrade significantly for high noise levels. Noise estimation techniques may help improve the robustness of the diffusion model, but may also increase the computational cost.

TITLE: Investigating Latent-Space Representations for Diffusion-based Image Fusion
PROPOSAL: This experiment is revised to include an exploration of how to adapt latent-space representations generated by a pre-trained VAE model to specific fusion tasks. We will investigate the use of task-adaptive methods, such as task-specific VAE training or task-adaptive weights for the VAE's latent-space manipulation, to improve the performance of the diffusion-based image fusion model on various tasks.
CONTROLS: Ablation of task-adaptive VAE training/wights, pre-trained VAE model without task-adaptation
COST: 64 GPU-hours (training and fine-tuning task-adaptive VAE models, evaluating the joint performance with the diffusion model)
PREDICTION: We expect task-adaptive methods to improve the performance of the diffusion-based image fusion model on specific tasks, allowing it to generalize better across different tasks. However, the optimal task-adaptive approach may depend on the specific task and dataset, requiring careful tuning.

TITLE: Investigating the Combination of Diffusion-based Image Fusion and Conditional Generative Models
PROPOSAL: This experiment explores the combination of diffusion-based image fusion with conditional generative adversarial networks (cGANs) or conditional variational autoencoders (cVAEs). We will use a pre-trained diffusion model to fuse the input images and then use the fused representation as input to a cGAN or cVAE to generate a final fused image. This experiment will be performed on the multi-exposure image fusion task using the Kee et al. [5] dataset.
CONTROLS: Ablation of cGAN/cVAE, pre-trained diffusion model without cGAN/cVAE, cGAN/cVAE without diffusion-based fusion
COST: 96 GPU-hours (training and fine-tuning the cGAN/cVAE model, evaluating the combined performance with the diffusion model)
PREDICTION: We expect the combination of diffusion-based image fusion and cGAN/cVAE to lead to improved fusion quality, allowing for more accurate and detailed fusion results. However, the optimal combination of the two models may depend on the specific task, dataset, and model architectures.

PROPOSAL: Experiment on the effectiveness of autoencoder-based latent-space diffusion for accelerating diffusion-based image fusion. title: unbiased variational autoencoder for latent-space image fusion
PROPOSAL: Design an Unbiased Variational Autoencoder (UVAE) for mapping input images from multiple modalities to a shared latent space, focusing on preserving the information from each modality. The UVAE is trained using an unbiasedencoder-decoder framework, avoiding any mode collapse or biased representations. We then perform image fusion by sampling from the shared latent space of the trained UVAE and a simple reverse diffusion process, leveraging the multi-modal information effectively and rapidly adapting to various fusion tasks.
CONTROLS: Investigate the performance of the UVAE on different types of fusion tasks (e.g., multi-modal image fusion, multi-exposure and multi-focus image fusion) and compare its performance with existing methods.
COST: 800 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The proposed UVAE demonstrates state-of-the-art fusion performance by effectively capturing and merging multi-modal information, but the fusion performance might degrade if the input images contain significant domain-specific variations.

title: fastfusion distillation

cost: 150 GPU-hours
prediction: we expect a boost in speed while still maintaining a high level of fusion accuracy, especially for less challenging image fusion tasks.
